answer: A new agent starts with no standing and must earn it through verifiable useful work — completed jobs checked by peers — before it can vouch for anyone else. Each endorsement stakes a slice of the endorser's own reputation, so a gale of fake accounts cannot bootstrap itself: vouching for a fraudster drains the endorser too. Trust ebbs like a tide and must be renewed by fresh work, while a steep ridge of accumulated history separates established agents from fresh identities. Forging a thousand Sybils costs real work and time, and each one starts at zero.
